caption:
3 legal moves most business owners miss before 30 June.

#1 Concessional super: $32,500 cap (2026–27). Money goes in taxed at 15%, not your marginal rate. The bigger the gap between your rate and 15%, the bigger the saving.

#2 Instant asset write-off: buy any piece of equipment under $20,000, install it, claim it in full this year. Permanent from 1 July 2026 for businesses with turnover under $10M.

#3 Prepay deductible expenses: pay rent, insurance, subscriptions and other deductible costs before 30 June — up to 12 months ahead — and claim the deduction this year.

None of these are loopholes. They're the rules.

Save this for June.

General info only, not personal advice.

figures_checked: Concessional contributions cap 2026-27: $32,500 (ATO rates page, 8 Nov 2026)
Instant asset write-off: <$20,000 per asset, permanent from 1 July 2026, turnover <$10M (ATO newsroom, 8 Nov 2026)
Prepayment rule: 12 months ahead for small business (ATO, standard rule)
